question: Does the 2026-10-16 RFC-BPR-0038 qualification-matrix amendment stand?
owner_answer_verbatim: Windows 11 and ubuntu wsl2 are tested. If it works on other things is unproven, but not disallowed
channel: Owner message in the coordinating session, relayed to the implementer verbatim; no attended-review session was opened for this one question

tested_environments.linux: Ubuntu 26.04 x86_64 under WSL2/WSLg on JaegAW
tested_environments.macos: unchanged: macOS 13+ universal, native Intel and Apple Silicon

other_environments: Unproven but not disallowed. Windows 10, other Linux distributions and native Linux desktops are not blocked, installs are not refused, and nothing claims them as tested or supported.
reading_of_the_2026_10_16_record: removed_requirements and claim_limit mean those environments leave the qualification matrix and the support claim. They do not add an install refusal, a platform check or a package floor change.
qualification_effect: None. This is wording and scope. No Windows 11 ordinary-user, WSL2/WSLg Secret Service, rendered, installer, removal, crash-privacy, vulnerability, trust or security-owner criterion is accepted. BPR-0958 to BPR-0962 stay Blocked, BPR-0973 stays Backlog and all nine RFC-BPR-0038 criteria remain open.
historical_records: The 2026-10-16 record stays byte-identical. Shipped release notes keep their original platform wording.
